audit.why: Levels 1-5 to Vladimir and Level 6 as the flip point matches the kits: Transfusion is 9s falling to 4.6s and Tides of Blood 13s falling to 5s, so his poke refreshes far faster than Arctic Assault's 18s or Winter's Wrath's 9s at rank 1. Glacial Prison at 1300 units is the first tool Sanguine Pool cannot answer on reaction. The shape of the lane is right; only the numbers inside it were wrong.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 2+ item spike names Vladimir's item scaling but never mentions Grievous Wounds, and Hemoplague is never named or timed anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Vladimir heals from two separate sources — Transfusion and Hemoplague, which heals him for every champion it hits — so the anti-heal buy is a spike in this matchup in its own right, and the entry omits it entirely. Hemoplague is 120s flat at every rank and amplifies the damage his team deals to everyone caught, which is exactly the fight Sejuani is trying to start with her own R.
audit.corrected: Buy Grievous Wounds by two items: Transfusion and Hemoplague both heal him. Hemoplague is 120s at every rank over 625 units.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (Transfusion heal; Hemoplague cd 120, range 625, 'heals Vladimir for each enemy Champion hit')

audit.whatIsWrong: Riot's own text for Tides of Blood says the released blood 'can be blocked by enemy units'. Neither layer mentions minion block anywhere, and the entry instead tells the player to 'farm under tower if you must' against that poke.
audit.why: This is the free answer to the ability the entry names as the reason levels 4-5 are unwinnable. Tides of Blood is his only ranged poke and it stops on the first unit it meets, so standing on the far side of your own melee minions turns his strongest lane tool off without conceding CS or tower position. The advice currently given — retreat under tower — costs farm to solve a problem that costs nothing to solve.
audit.corrected: Tides of Blood is blocked by enemy units — keep your own minions between you and him and his poke never reaches you.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (Tides of Blood: 'deals damage in the area around him but can be blocked by enemy units')

audit.whatIsWrong: Fury of the North's Frost Armor grants immunity to slows. Vladimir's only two slows are Sanguine Pool and Tides of Blood. Neither layer mentions it, and whys[6] instead sells his Rylai's slow as part of why he is uncatchable.
audit.why: Every approach in this lane starts with a Sejuani who has been standing in the wave out of combat, so Frost Armor is up and the first Tides of Blood slow simply does not hold her. That changes the approach rule from 'you cannot walk at him' to 'you can walk at him once, on the buff'. Selling his slows as the reason he escapes is the exact opposite of what the passive does.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor makes you immune to slows out of combat, so his Tides of Blood and Rylai's slows do nothing on your first step-up — that step is your window.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (Fury of the North: 'Frost Armor which grants Armor and Magic Resist and immunity to slows')
champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (slow flags on W and E)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] states Sanguine Pool has a '26-second CD'. It is 28/25/22/19/16 seconds. 26 is not a value at any rank.
audit.why: The entry calls that number 'your engagement timer', so the single number the whole plan depends on is wrong at every rank. At rank 1 the player under-counts by two seconds and walks in early; by rank 5 he over-counts by ten and never walks in at all.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer twice credits Sejuani's armour to 'your passive Permafrost armor bonus'. Permafrost is her E stun and has no passive; the armour and MR come from Frost Armor on Fury of the North.
audit.why: Frost Armor only exists after Sejuani has been out of combat and it falls off shortly after she takes damage. Attaching it to Permafrost erases that condition, so a player believes the resistances are always there and steps into extended poke expecting stats he does not have.
audit.corrected: The resistances are Frost Armor from Fury of the North, gained out of combat and lost shortly after taking damage.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (Fury of the North and Permafrost descriptions)

edits.after: Force trades only when Sanguine Pool is down — 28/25/22/19/16s is your real engagement timer

edits.after: Poke with Transfusion (Q), but Tides of Blood is blocked by units — keep minions between you

edits.before: Full AP Vladimir drains through your resistances and Sanguine Pool makes every targeted CC attempt a wasted cooldown — peel for allies rather than chasing him.
edits.after: Buy Grievous Wounds by now — Transfusion and Hemoplague both heal him — and remember Sanguine Pool's two untargetable seconds eat any Permafrost you try to land.

edits.before: Crimson Rush empowered Q Transfusion heals him for more than your poke trades can inflict and his E Tides of Blood strips your passive Permafrost armor — concede and farm.
edits.after: His empowered Transfusion heals more than your poke can take off, but Tides of Blood is blocked by enemy units — stand behind your own minions and it never reaches you.

edits.before: Full AP Vladimir with Rylai's slow and Sanguine Pool makes him nearly unkillable in a straight chase — your job is to land R to burn the Pool, then let your team clean up.
edits.after: Frost Armor makes you slow-immune out of combat, so his Rylai's and Pool slows miss your first step — land R to burn the Pool, then let your team clean up.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 belong to Vladimir: Crimson Rush empowers his Q Transfusion into a healing drain that chunks you, and his E Tides of Blood poke reaches far enough to strip your passive Permafrost armor bonus before you close. Farm under tower if you must and do not trade until Pool is on cooldown. At level 6, Glacial Prison changes the equation entirely — throw R from outside his reaction window, walk into the blizzard zone, and chain Q into W-E while he is stunned; Sanguine Pool cannot be activated while he is CC'd by the initial projectile hit, only the blizzard slow.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 belong to Vladimir: his empowered Transfusion is a healing drain that chunks you, and Tides of Blood strips the Frost Armor resistances off Fury of the North before you close. Keep your own minions between you — Riot's text says that blood is blocked by enemy units — and do not trade until Pool is down, 28s at rank 1. At level 6, Glacial Prison changes the equation entirely: throw R from outside his reaction window, walk into the blizzard, and chain Q into W-E while he is stunned. He cannot pool while the projectile stun holds him, only through the blizzard slow.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your Q dash like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: 28/25/22/19/16s — two untargetable seconds, so bait it out before you spend your kill window. - Hemoplague: 120s at every rank, and it heals him per champion hit. - Guard your Q like a fifth summoner spell.

notes: Best find: Riot's own Tides of Blood text says it 'can be blocked by enemy units'. The entry names that poke as the reason levels 4-5 are unplayable and tells the player to farm under tower; standing behind his own melee minions solves it for free. Second: wants.you[1] gives Sanguine Pool a '26-second CD' and calls it 'your engagement timer' — the real values are 28/25/22/19/16, so the one number the plan hangs on is wrong at every rank. Third: Frost Armor grants immunity to slows and Vladimir's only slows are Pool and Tides of Blood, which whys[6] currently sells as the reason he is uncatchable. UNVERIFIED, left alone: the entry uses 'Crimson Rush' three times for Vladimir's full-resource Transfusion empowerment. Data Dragon names the passive Crimson Pact and does not name the empowerment at all, so I could not confirm or refute 'Crimson Rush' from the kit files and did not touch it — flagging rather than guessing. NOT EDITED: 'passive Permafrost armor bonus' still appears in wants.foe[1]-adjacent prose and early; the applier should sweep that phrase. The suspectNames hits on 'Sanguine Pool' and 'Glacial Prison' are FALSE POSITIVES — the detector matched the leading word, the ability names are correct.
